title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East  (Late Show) on 1970-05-15
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > ZA2 > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard recording that captures a legendary May 15 1970 Fillmore East marathon – flawless acoustic sets, powerhouse electric jams and standout Dark Star/The Other One.
ai_review.review: This SBD from the early‑late show on May 15 1970 delivers crystal‑clear audio with only occasional hiss or tiny dropouts, letting the band’s eclectic setlist shine.  Highlights include a soaring Dark Star, a monster The Other One, superb acoustic renditions of Friend of the Devil and Candyman, plus tight New Riders of the Purple Sage interludes.  Jerry’s guitar (even pedal‑steel), Phil’s thunderous bass, Bob’s vocal banter and Pigpen’s organ all receive glowing mentions.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 80 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and audio; minor glitches are noted but do not detract from an overall near‑perfect experience.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp mix with superb instrument separation; occasional faint hiss or tiny cuts in a few tracks but no major dropouts.  The SBD captures both acoustic intimacy and electric power.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two full acoustic sets bookend New Riders interludes and two electric sets, creating a seamless marathon that moves from folk‑rock intimacy to psychedelic jams without loss of momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring lead guitar, flawless vocals and even pedal‑steel on the NRPS set; multiple reviewers call his playing "outstanding" and "the best ever".
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a thunderous bass line that drives The Other One and Dark Star; percussion contributions highlighted as essential to the 1970 vibe.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby’s banter, vocal harmonies and acoustic rhythm work are repeatedly described as amusing and solid; his organ/tapestry on Cold Jordan gets special praise.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard support (Pigpen’s organ) is called “tapestry” that backs jams like Cold Jordan; overall keys are seen as tight and complementary.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s drumming receives commendations for spacey effects in Dark Star and solid groove throughout the electric sets.
